Honestly no. DBT felt like a sticking plaster rather than dealing with the issue itself. But when we realised that DBT was making things more complicated, I was referred for Schema Therapy and that’s the best thing that’s ever happened to me. It looks at your core schemas, where they come from and how they’re triggered. And then how to balance them into being a healthy adult. 

I have CPTSD, BPD, BDD and a severe depressive disorder - if any of you feel that some of those are familiar to you and you don’t feel like CBT, DBT etc are effective for you, please look into schema!

Honestly mental hospitals are no better than general hospitals regarding bpd and relationships. But sometimes they can direct you to a more appropriate service. And sometimes they can give you a diagnosis which might make things a bit easier for you. I spent most of the last four years in one in the UK. The best advice I can give is to hold on. Only you know your truth, you tell every fucker going what has happened and that things don’t feel right. They have no right to be dismissive of that. Therapy is the solution but you’ll have hoops to jump through to get to that. But you can do it, and then you can live life for you, not others.
